chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Musa ibn al-Hasan from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Fadalah ibn Ayub, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has lifted from the women four [obligations]: the vocalizing of the Talbiyah, the Sa'i between As-Safa and al-Marwah, entering the Ka'bah, and the Istilam (kissing or touching the Black Stone).

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: The vocal declaration of 'Labbayk' during Hajj
key_terms.السَّعْيَ: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.الِاسْتِلَامَ: The act of kissing or touching the Black Stone
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cubic building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What are the four Hajj rituals that women are exempted from according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies four ritual acts of Hajj that are exempted for women: reciting the Talbiah aloud, performing Sa'i, entering the Ka'bah, and Istilam. This exemption reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *rukhnah* (divine leniency) based on women's natural state, distinguishing their ritual performance from the full obligations required of men.
